chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Natana (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), he said:
"Whoever mentions the name of God over food will never be asked about the blessing of that food."

key_terms.الطعام: Food — here representing all forms of divine provision and sustenance
key_terms.ذكر اسم الله: Mentioning the name of God (saying bismillah) — the practice of invoking God's name before eating
key_terms.نعيم: Bounty, blessing, or favor — refers to the divine provision that will be subject to accounting on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of saying bismillah before eating according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through a chain reaching Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), teaches that mentioning God's name (saying bismillah) before eating ensures that the person will not be questioned on the Day of Judgment about the bounty of that food. This connects to the Quranic concept in Surah al-Takathur (102:8), where God says people will be questioned about their blessings. By invoking God's name, one acknowledges the source of the provision and demonstrates gratitude, thereby fulfilling the duty of thankfulness.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: 13. Al-Husayn b. Ibrahim Natana (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Yahya al-Khazzaz from Ghiyath b. Ibrahim from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from `Ali b. Abi Talib (a.s.), he said: "
Whoever mentions the name of Allah over food will never be asked about the blessing of that food."
